analysis.evidence: Canaan fathers Sidon and Heth. The phrase צִידֹן בְּכֹרוֹ “Sidon his firstborn” identifies Canaan as a father in the genealogy.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וּ “and” prefixes the personal name כְּנַעַן, the subject of יָלַד “fathered.”

analysis.evidence: Carried forward: this word and its source tagging were reviewed identically at 68109:1, 68104:1, 66578:5, 66578:9, 66578:13.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person masculine singular, with no prefix or suffix

analysis.evidence: אֶת introduces צִידֹן (Sidon) as the direct object of יָלַד (fathered). בְּכֹרוֹ (his firstborn) identifies Sidon, and וְאֶת חֵת marks Heth as the second object of the same verb.
analysis.morphology: Direct-object particle with no prefix or suffix.

evidence.note: In אֶת צִידֹן בְּכֹרוֹ, “Sidon his firstborn,” the writer identifies Sidon as Canaan’s firstborn child.

article.name: צִידֹן
article.summary: Genesis 10:15 names Sidon as Canaan’s firstborn son. The meaning of his name is uncertain.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for צִידֹן. The packet’s gloss “Levi” conflicts with the name in the verse, and the text gives no support for the proposed root צחר.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:15 names צִידֹן as the child Canaan fathered and calls him בְּכֹרוֹ, “his firstborn.”

analysis.evidence: In וּכְנַעַן יָלַד אֶת צִידֹן בְּכֹרוֹ, Canaan is the father, and בְּכֹרוֹ (“his firstborn”) identifies Sidon’s relationship to him. The verse gives no etymology for the name.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no prefix or suffix. The preceding אֶת is a separate word marking the direct object of יָלַד.
analysis.sense: The personal name of Canaan’s firstborn son.

analysis.evidence: Canaan is the subject of יָלַד ‘fathered’. בְּכֹרוֹ stands in apposition to צִידֹן, identifying Sidon as Canaan’s firstborn son.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular common noun in the construct state with a third-person masculine singular possessive suffix referring to Canaan.

evidence.note: “Canaan fathered Sidon his firstborn, and Heth.” The phrase וְאֶת חֵת names another son of Canaan.

article.name: חֵת
article.summary: Heth is named after Sidon among Canaan’s children. The name’s etymology is uncertain.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for חֵת. The candidate חַת means “dread” and has a different vowel.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:15 identifies Heth by descent from Canaan and gives no explanation of the name’s origin.

analysis.evidence: The repeated object marker in יָלַד אֶת צִידֹן בְּכֹרוֹ וְאֶת חֵת places Heth alongside Sidon as a second child whom Canaan fathered.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no prefix or suffix. The preceding וְאֶת is a separate word.
